# Codex history service

Arcane records sanitized public native history for the current acknowledged project-bound Codex thread. Cached history remains readable after daemon restart, with no provider launch or restored execution permissions.

## HTTP/action contract for UI integration

Both routes use the existing human control bearer, exact Host, no query parameters, no-store responses, and existing Origin checks. Agent bearers receive HUMAN_ONLY (403). A POST requires the exact application Origin and application/json. The trusted project path, provider executable, session ID, parser options and native history payload are never browser input.

Human refresh uses the existing POST /v1/codex/action endpoint:

~~~json
{
  "requestId": "<fresh UUID>",
  "action": "history-load",
  "connectionId": "<exact live connection UUID>",
  "threadId": "<nativeHistory.threadId>"
}
~~~

The response remains {record, replayed, state}. Successful reads return 200 with an acknowledged action receipt, including incomplete histories with visible gap evidence. Refused reads return 409 with a rejected receipt. Existing pre-action envelope/idempotency/authentication errors retain their existing statuses. A crash-pending receipt may be classified unknown on restart; it is never automatically dispatched again. Reusing the same request ID returns its existing receipt without another native read; a new human refresh needs a fresh ID.

The service state and every normal action response carry nativeHistory:

~~~typescript
nativeHistory: null | {
  projectPath: string;
  threadId: string;
  sessionId: string | null;
  recorded: null | {
    requestId: string;
    connectionId: string;
    provenance: 'installed-cli' | 'spawned-node-fixture';
    loadedAt: string; // ISO timestamp of this recording, not proof of current native contents
    result: {
      entries: Array<{
        role: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'tool';
        text: string;
        ids: { threadId: string; sessionId: string | null; turnId: string; itemId: string };
      }>;
      completeness: 'complete' | 'incomplete' | 'rejected';
      gaps: Array<{reason: HistoryGapReason; turnId?: string; itemId?: string}>;
      truncated: boolean;
      marker: string | null;
      excludedItems: number;
      droppedGaps: number;
      redacted: boolean;
    };
  };
}
~~~

Recorded results have completeness complete or incomplete. Rejected parser results cannot replace a previous verified recording. Incomplete results carry the existing history gap marker. An empty hydrated legacy history can be complete; an empty paginated read remains incomplete because it does not establish hydration. Excluded private item kinds do not imply a missing public message. Data is a recording, not an execution permission or a live transcript cursor.

GET /v1/codex/history returns {nativeHistory} from the local cache. GET /v1/codex/state also includes nativeHistory. These reads remain inert after restart: snapshot and lastSnapshot stay null until explicit lifecycle actions. A recorded thread can be refreshed after a human explicitly reconnects, even when that connection has no selected model and no resumed thread. History refresh itself never connects or resumes. A live connection with another thread cannot read the recorded binding.

## Native wire and scope

Implementation was checked against public TypeScript bindings generated by installed codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 using codex app-server generate-ts --out <unique temporary directory>. ThreadReadParams declares threadId and includeTurns; ThreadReadResponse declares thread. Thread distinguishes sessionId, cwd, ephemeral, historyMode and turns.

The lifecycle transport excludes thread/read and is outside this task's write scope. CodexSession.readThreadHistory therefore starts a one-shot reader using the trusted host process specification. That reader sends initialize, initialized and exactly one thread/read with {threadId, includeTurns:true}. It closes after the response, error, timeout, disconnect or shutdown. Cleanup settles on actual child exit (or a bounded kill deadline) and destroys pipes, so Windows close-event lag cannot hold a completed read indefinitely. It does not send account/read, model/list, thread/start, thread/resume or turn/start. Unknown native server requests are refused; no tool or approval can be accepted by the reader. No experimental pagination is negotiated.

The daemon admits only its single current binding, recorded on an acknowledged thread/start or thread/resume. Binding is keyed by the canonical trusted project path. The parser checks exact native thread ID, optional recorded session ID and exact project cwd before visiting content. It rejects foreign projects/threads/sessions, ephemeral threads, unknown history modes and pagination envelopes. Paginated thread/read compatibility is gated by the response evidence described below. A new acknowledged current thread clears the previous thread's projection. A different project cannot display or refresh that recording.

## Paginated response evidence

The historyMode label alone does not establish whether thread/read returned a hydrated public projection. For an explicit includeTurns:true request, a paginated ThreadReadResponse can be projected when it contains a nonempty turns array and the inspected turns explicitly report itemsView:'full'. User, assistant and recognized tool text then follow the same exact-scope checks, native IDs, exclusions, redaction and bounds as legacy responses. This conditional projection does not advertise general paginated-history support, fetch older pages, or prove that every native page was returned.

Each paginated turn must independently supply itemsView:'full' before its items are visited. A summary view or a missing view produces items-not-full gap evidence and its content is omitted. Empty paginated turns or missing turns remain incomplete with a gap marker; they cannot be reported as a complete empty native conversation. In a mixed response, valid full turns can contribute entries while summary/missing-view turns keep the recording incomplete. Unknown historyMode values and cursor/page envelopes are rejected even if embedded items resemble valid full turns. No pagination API, resume action, inference, or write grant is triggered to fill gaps.

The parent reported a metadata observation of a completed paginated turn with explicit full items and public user/assistant/MCP/reasoning item kinds. The service fixtures reproduce that shape using synthetic IDs and text. This document does not claim genuine installed-CLI verification from those fixtures; the parent's final metadata proof is still required.

## Durability and bounds

Schema version 2 adds a singleton native_history table to Arcane's own codex-actions.sqlite journal. One binding and one recording are retained. Binding/projection and acknowledged receipt are committed in the same SQLite transaction. Startup never connects, resumes, rereads, or replays native work. Version 1 receipts migrate intact without guessing a project binding from historical action receipts; a subsequent explicit acknowledged thread action establishes one.

The existing parser projects recognized public user, assistant and tool text only, preserving exact IDs. It excludes reasoning/private kinds and never stores raw native envelopes, preview, transcript paths, command arguments, structured tool content, or stderr. Recognized credential forms are redacted before SQLite storage, and cached projections are validated and redacted again on retrieval. Redaction is defense in depth, not detection of every possible arbitrary secret. HTTP continues to remove the known control and agent bearers from serialized responses.

Limits remain fixed or reducible: 64 turns, 256 inspected items, 2 MiB projected result, bounded gaps, plus at most 16 KiB recording metadata. The one-shot reader inherits the native client's 1 MiB frame limit, aggregate output/stderr bounds, queue bound and request deadline; a wire frame above that limit is refused rather than advertised as complete. Missing turns, omitted non-text/unknown items, failed/unfinished turns, compaction and parser limits retain explicit incomplete-history evidence. A rejected/failed/stale read preserves the previous recording. Disconnect and shutdown cancel readers; receipt replay never repeats a read.

## Targeted verification

The new tests/unit/codex-history-service.test.ts creates labelled Node protocol fixtures and SQLite journals only in verified unique temporary directories. It covers inert/human-only endpoints, exact wire shape, IDs, redaction before persistence, restart retrieval, reconnect-without-resume refresh, request replay, scope rejection, evidence-gated paginated full projections, incomplete paginated summary/missing-view/empty responses, unknown-mode/page-envelope rejection, bounds/gaps, unsolicited approval refusal, busy/disconnect/shutdown/timeout handling, project isolation, current-thread replacement and v1 migration.

Focused compilation/test output is isolated in a unique system temporary directory. Relevant regression entrypoints are codex-history.test.ts, codex-client.test.ts and codex-http.test.ts. No shared build, packaging, root test suite, native authentication, native model inference, Studio or paid tooling is required. Genuine installed-CLI history execution and desktop UI integration remain unverified by these synthetic fixtures.

Previous baseline verification (before the paginated compatibility update): strict TypeScript compilation of the four explicit Codex test entrypoints and their imported dependencies passed. Tests passed: 27 history service tests, 30 existing parser tests, and 99 existing client/HTTP tests (156 total; zero failures). After final reader cleanup, the focused compile and 27 service tests passed again. Scoped git diff --check passed. Compile output remained in a unique system temporary directory; no shared build or packaging ran.

Paginated compatibility verification: pending focused temporary compilation and fixture execution against the parent-owned parser update. Only tests/unit/codex-history-service.test.ts and this document are owned by the sidecar update; production parser edits and genuine CLI metadata proof belong to the parent.
